overview: Reward and motivation are mediated by midbrain dopamine neurons — principally in the ventral tegmental area (and substantia nigra pars compacta) — that project via the mesolimbic pathway to the nucleus accumbens and amygdala, and via the mesocortical pathway to the prefrontal cortex. Dopamine signals reward prediction error, driving learning and incentive salience; dysregulation of these pathways underlies addiction and several psychiatric disorders.

citations.source: Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science, 6th ed. (2021), Ch. 49
Purves et al., Neuroscience, 5th ed. (2012), Ch. 29

function: Midbrain dopaminergic cell groups (A9 substantia nigra pars compacta, alongside the A10 ventral tegmental area) that are the source of ascending dopamine.
Dopamine encodes reward-prediction error — firing phasically when outcomes exceed expectation — and reinforces actions that led to reward.

clinical.note: Drugs of abuse converge on elevating dopamine in the nucleus accumbens, hijacking reward learning.
SNc degeneration depletes dorsal-striatal dopamine, causing motor signs (nigrostriatal pathway).

function: Ventral striatal hub of the mesolimbic pathway; integrates dopamine and glutamatergic (prefrontal, hippocampal, amygdala) inputs to drive motivation and reward-seeking.
Encodes incentive salience ('wanting'), value, and effort-based decision-making.

clinical.note: Blunted accumbens reward responses correlate with anhedonia; drug craving correlates with accumbens dopamine release.

function: Assigns emotional value to sensory stimuli and projects to the nucleus accumbens, gating reward-seeking by learned affective significance.
Links reward memory with the dopamine system during conditioned reinforcement.

clinical.note: BLA→accumbens projections drive the motivational pull of drug-associated cues.

function: Ventromedial prefrontal / orbitofrontal territory implicated in reward value representation, reversal learning, and outcome-guided decision-making.
Part of the mesocortical target network that flexibly updates stimulus–reward associations.

clinical.note: Orbitofrontal dysfunction impairs reversal learning and contributes to compulsive drug-seeking despite adverse consequences.

function: Anterior/mid-cingulate target of the mesocortical dopamine pathway; encodes the effort and cost of actions and integrates reward value with cognitive control.
Tracks the 'work' required to obtain reward and signals prediction errors during learning.

clinical.note: Reduced mesocortical dopamine to the anterior cingulate correlates with motivational deficits in depression and schizophrenia.

questions.stem: What does the phasic firing of midbrain dopamine neurons encode?
questions.explanation: Dopamine neurons fire phasically when reward exceeds prediction, is unchanged at fully predicted reward, and pause when reward is omitted — the reward-prediction-error signal.

questions.stem: Which structure is the ventral-striatal hub of the mesolimbic dopamine pathway?
questions.explanation: The nucleus accumbens is the core of the ventral striatum and the primary mesolimbic target of VTA dopamine neurons.

questions.stem: Which pathway projects dopamine from the VTA to the prefrontal cortex?
questions.explanation: The mesocortical pathway conveys VTA dopamine to the prefrontal cortex (including anterior cingulate and orbitofrontal regions), modulating cognition and motivation.

questions.stem: Find the ventral-striatal hub of the mesolimbic reward pathway.
questions.explanation: The nucleus accumbens is the core of the ventral striatum and the main target of the mesolimbic dopamine pathway.
